plan: Store the workspace as a single deep-copied nested dict; deep-copy again in to_data() so callers can never alias internal state.
Provide one recursive depth-first generator (_iter_items) over all items; implement total_word_count and unresolved_markers as folds over it that dispatch on item kind (note vs reference).

Use one compiled marker regex \[\[\?([^\[\]]+?)\]\] for both extracting marker identifiers and stripping markers (replaced by a space) before counting words with \b\w+\b, so marker syntax and identifiers never count as words.
Render outline() with a recursive walker that appends '  ' * depth + '<kind>: <title>' lines under the workspace title, giving deterministic output from list order.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: check id types, locate the item and its parent list, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a section/group item), reject non-containers, reject self/descendant destinations via a subtree scan, and range-check the insertion index against the destination length; only after all checks pass, pop from the source list and insert/append into the destination. Because no mutation precedes the final check, any ValueError leaves to_data() exactly unchanged.
mechanisms: Deep-copy isolation at construction and export boundaries (copy.deepcopy in __init__ and to_data)
Single recursive depth-first traversal generator shared by all aggregate queries
Kind-based dispatch for summary contributions (note text parsing vs reference declared word_count/unresolved)
Compiled regex pair: marker pattern for extraction and removal, word pattern for counting
Set accumulation plus sorted() for unique lexicographic marker identifiers
Depth-tracked recursive outline renderer using two-space indentation per nesting level
Parent-list/index locator (_find) returning (container_list, position, item) for structural edits
Validate-then-mutate move protocol guaranteeing atomicity of failed moves
Subtree membership scan to reject moves of a container into itself or its descendants
Explicit insertion-index bounds check (0 through destination length) before any list mutation
